searchText: Sorry for sending the last messages they were not supposed to be send here <@213402680637259777> I just merged your PR for the docker build Nice work Good stuff. It looks like the action ran successfully, but I can't find the image repo at https://hub.docker.com/shresthagrawal/kevlar I can see it here https://hub.docker.com/r/shresthagrawal/kevlar Aha. Cool. I tried searching it, but I guess their search cache isn't updated. thats weird though Also `docker run -p 8546:8546 --name kevlar shresthagrawal/kevlar` doesn't work but this `docker run -p 8546:8546 --name kevlar shresthagrawal/kevlar:main` works Yeah, you'll need to tag a version in semver format The metadata builder sets latest to whatever the latest tagged version is aah, so it will be there in the next release Indeed. You could tag a revision to an existing release to trigger the action automatically, I think. Not sure if there's a button you can push to do it without tagging Anyways I will do a patch release soon <@563394111214714881> Before I embark on figuring it out myself, have you given any consideration to how to make Patronum's proofs efficiently portable? I'm thinking of creating a protobuf serialization of the needed data, efficiently compressed where possible. It might also be interesting to reproducibly compile the EVM simulation of the RPC call into a portable WASM That way, RPC gateways - or other gateways that need to show their work - can take on the heavy lifting, and the client can just run their semi-trusted verifier I haven't really started working on the optimization side of Patronum. For now I was trying to make sure its stable and has full RPC support first I don't think it's fully stable. Sometimes the gas estimates are off. Also we are missing few RPC endpoints I did think about implementing everything in Rust to make it very light weight but never got time to do it Hey Justin! I made a proposal at the light clients workshop at Devcon regarding this, hoping to consolidate some feedback from people working in the light client dev ecosystem about how to go about this. Unfortunately, the audio did not get recorded, but here are the slides from the presentation: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1fKfsGYEYoLWoZGFjtKeLjSU8wa8GRx1brf9CvMu1LWU/edit?usp=sharing TL;DR: I'm looking to see how we can better persist, discuss and collaborate all our efforts in this part of the ecosystem and to create a better DevEx for those looking to contribute to this effort. I'm going to start with creating a wiki of information (likely using Notion) about this ecosystem, what people are working on and references to everyone's contributed efforts. Currently, we have a github repo (https://github.io/ethereum-light-clients), Twitter (https://twitter.com/ethlightclients), Telegram Announcements (https://t.me/+vKomz6woYTBkNGIx), Discord (this channel) and central domain (https://lightclients.xyz) - which will likely become the new wiki page.

excerpts.author: philngo
excerpts.content:
Hey Justin! I made a proposal at the light clients workshop at Devcon regarding this, hoping to consolidate some feedback from people working in the light client dev ecosystem about how to go about this. Unfortunately, the audio did not get recorded, but here are the slides from the presentation:
https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1fKfsGYEYoLWoZGFjtKeLjSU8wa8GRx1brf9CvMu1LWU/edit?usp=sharing

TL;DR: I'm looking to see how we can better persist, discuss and collaborate all our efforts in this part of the ecosystem and to create a better DevEx for those looking to contribute to this effort. I'm going to start with creating a wiki of information (likely using Notion) about this ecosystem, what people are working on and references to everyone's contributed efforts.

Currently, we have a github repo (https://github.io/ethereum-light-clients), Twitter (https://twitter.com/ethlightclients), Telegram Announcements (https://t.me/+vKomz6woYTBkNGIx), Discord (this channel) and central domain (https://lightclients.xyz) - which will likely become the new wiki page.
